correctness.rationale: The circular maximum can always start at one. For a weight-four root, the second and fourth one threshold minima force the following gap to be minimum and preceding gap maximum, which also minimizes the sum of two consecutive gaps and hence the third threshold. This proves the exact root set for every four-gap tuple. The forbidden necklace enumeration uses all four nontrivial rank multiplicities with orbit size exactly four, producing the rational GF. Burnside and poles yield limiting 2/3. The explicit k>=5 gap family disproves the naive extension for all larger weights; the finite checker independently confirms root sets on 14,950 tuples, 23 coefficients and weight-five boundary. Finite checks are not an unbounded proof.

Existing three-marker and four-run results intersect only smaller or different parameter families, and the general rearrangement theorem allows transformations other than rotation. A possibility of unindexed equivalent work remains; no independent priority certification is asserted.

value.rationale: The exact criterion answers a natural canonical circular rotation question in jumbled indexing for all binary circles with exactly four markers, including ties, zero gaps and nonprimitive words. Its forbidden-necklace rational series and limiting nonexistence frequency 2/3 are nontrivial natural invariants; a uniform higher-weight counterexample identifies the precise point where the extremal adjacency criterion ceases to suffice. These facts are neither a table lookup nor a routine substitution in the three-marker theorem.
